clippings.speaker: Emmanuel Lubezki
clippings.quote: I met Alfonso many, many years ago. We went as teenagers to the same parties, talked about the same girls, we danced together, and we went to film theaters together. We spent many hours watching what you guys call foreign films in the late 70s and early 80s, and he was always a little bit of a teacher for me. We’re almost on the same frequency–sometimes he doesn’t call me for a year, but when he calls and says, ‘Oh I have this idea for this movie,’ it just happens to be exactly what I would like to be doing.
clippings.title: One of the Greatest Cinematographers Ever: Gravity's Emmanuel Lubezki
clippings.context: Lubezki, asked in a Gravity-season interview with the MPA's blog whether growing up together explains their partnership.

clippings.speaker: Emmanuel Lubezki
clippings.quote: I think that’s important in our relationship, that there’s a level of honesty that can be brutal. Like Alfonso will see me lighting and he’ll come around and say, “Is this really your lighting?” And I’ll say, “Is this your shitty blocking?” But usually when he approaches and he makes that comment, he’s 100% right.
clippings.context: Lubezki at the Tribeca Talks conversation with Cuarón, on the blunt honesty between them.
clippings.title: Alfonso Cuarón and Emmanuel Lubezki Relive the Funniest Moments From 30 Years of Making Films Together

clippings.speaker: Emmanuel Lubezki
clippings.quote: And I saw the most amazing, one of the greatest moments of Alfonso improvising, like a jazz player at the top of his game. … and he opened the window and put snow, and suddenly in one hour he figured out my favorite scene of the movie, and it’s improvised. And I think it’s only possible because you were a mature filmmaker at that point.
clippings.context: Lubezki at the Tribeca Talks conversation, recalling the improvised snow-through-the-window scene when the budget for petals fell through.
clippings.title: Alfonso Cuarón and Emmanuel Lubezki Relive the Funniest Moments From 30 Years of Making Films Together

clippings.speaker: Alfonso Cuarón
clippings.quote: Chivo sometimes makes these comments and you don’t know if he’s pulling your leg or if he’s actually genuinely serious or concerned, or if he’s mocking you. But one day we were looking for locations for the show, and he said, “What do you want to do after this? Do you want to direct soaps?” And I said, “Why?” And it was the same company that produced all the soaps, “I see that you’re so committed here that maybe that’s your thing, and that’s fine.” But he completely shook my ground because suddenly I realized, “Wow, I’m getting a bit too comfy here.”
clippings.context: Cuarón at the Tribeca Talks conversation, on a location scout for the TV series Hora Marcada when Lubezki asked if he wanted to direct soaps.
clippings.title: Alfonso Cuarón and Emmanuel Lubezki Relive the Funniest Moments From 30 Years of Making Films Together

clippings.speaker: Alfonso Cuarón
clippings.quote: That film was a turning point for me. After that film I was not happy. … And that’s when I called you to do Y tu mamá también. … We talked about let’s do the film that we would have done before we went to film school.
clippings.context: Cuarón at the Tribeca Talks conversation, on Great Expectations flopping and calling Lubezki to make Y tu mamá también.
clippings.title: Alfonso Cuarón and Emmanuel Lubezki Relive the Funniest Moments From 30 Years of Making Films Together

clippings.speaker: Alfonso Cuarón
clippings.quote: Embracing being a cinematographer forced me to be on the set all day long. When we work together, we work, I go away. Somehow I had to be there, that was triggering more details of the memory of the moment, it was very useful. I was there lighting, and composing. For me, it was: “What would Chivo do?”
clippings.title: Cuarón Tells Lubezki How He Filmed ‘Roma’ — Even One Quiet Shot Needed 45 Camera Positions
clippings.context: Cuarón onstage at Raleigh Studios, answering Lubezki's questions about shooting Roma himself after Lubezki had to drop out.
